facts.statement: The genus Akaimia was first described by Jan Rees in 2010.
facts.quote: It was first named by Jan Rees in 2010.

facts.statement: The type species, A. altucuspis, lived during the middle or late Jurassic in southern Poland.
facts.quote: the type species A. altucuspis from the middle or late Jurassic (Callovian or Oxfordian age) of Ogrodzieniec near Zawiercie, southern Poland

facts.statement: The species A. myriacuspis lived during the middle Jurassic in the Oxford Clay near Peterborough.
facts.quote: A. myriacuspis, from the middle Jurassic (Callovian) of the Oxford Clay, near Peterborough.

facts.statement: Akaimia belongs to the parent group Orectolobiformes.
Akaimia is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.
Akaimia lived between 165.3 and 161.5 million years ago during the Callovian age.
facts.quote: Time range: Callovian to Callovian (165.3 to 161.5 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Akaimia is an extinct genus of carpet sharks that lived across Europe.
rejected.quote: Akaimia is an extinct genus of carpet sharks which existed across Europe.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'Akaimia is an extinct genus of carpet sharks'
